header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Chen (Redwood SE) -- Marta Lopez (Brighton Head of Security), Ethan Green (Brighton CTO), Sofia Rivera (Compliance), Liam O'Brien (Platform)
summary: Brighton Therapy wants to confirm that Redwood can guarantee EU-only processing for certain workloads, understand cross-border fallbacks, review subprocessor onboarding, and validate KMS/crypto controls. AE/SE explained routing, VPC/private deployment options, and KMS integration. Agreed next steps: share subprocessor inventory and SOC2/ISO artifacts, schedule technical deep-dive to prove region pinning and run a small pilot routing test.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run through Brighton's questions around region pinning and your compliance ask. Quick intros?
[00:10] Marta (Brighton): Hi, Marta here. Head of Security, I'll mostly be listening for data residency and subprocessor commitments.
[00:16] Ethan (Brighton): Ethan, CTO, we'll cover networking and routing.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. Priya and Noah from infra are on the call to take the deep tech questions. Priya, wanna kick off with a short overview of Redwood's routing model?
[00:30] Priya (Redwood): Sure. So, at a high level we have a control plane that routes requests to the closest serving plane based on policy: by default region affinity tries to keep tokens local, but we support hard region pinning where requests are only ever served in EU or US. There's also automatically triggered fallback rules if capacity is constrained–we can fail closed or route to a compatible variant.
[00:52] Marta: When you say "hard pinning" is that a contractual guarantee or a best-effort? We need EU-only for certain PHI-related call transcripts.
[01:00] Jordan: Good q. Contractually we can offer region pinning as part of a dedicated/private deployment SLA. For hosted accounts we offer region affinity with strong controls, plus signed attestation and subprocessor commitments. For EU-only processing we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated so you get explicit no-cross-border clauses.
[01:22] Sofia (Brighton): If we go Dedicated, do you provision in our VPC or is it still via Redwood-managed infra in eu-west-1?
[01:30] Priya: Two options. Dedicated reserved capacity can be Redwood-managed but logically isolated by tenancy and region-locked; Private (VPC) lets you manage the network and we push the serving runtime into your VPC. Both can be configured with customer-managed KMS (we'll talk KM S later).
[01:48] Ethan: Can you describe the KMS flow? We need to know whether keys ever leave our control or are rewrapped by Redwood.
[01:55] Noah: Short answer: we support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys in major cloud KMS providers. With customer-managed keys, the cryptographic root material stays in your K M S; Redwood performs envelope encryption and the unwrapping happens within the same region where the keys live. We do not exfiltrate raw keys.
[02:20] Marta: OK but what about backups or model caches? If you cache prefixes or KV cache, could that be replicated cross-border?
[02:28] Priya: Good catch. By default KV cache is colocated with the serving plane; with region pinning we ensure caches stay in-region. Backups for stateful components are stored per-region and we can disable cross-region backups for Private deployments. For hosted, backup replication is documented in the subprocessor and infra map; we can exclude certain data classes from cross-region replication via config.
[02:52] Liam (Brighton): How do you prove this? We need evidence for audit: logs, traces, and a map of subprocessors and their regions.
[03:00] Jordan: We'll provide SOC2 artifacts, ISO attestation, and a subprocessor inventory with region mapping. We'll also provide example audit logs and a tracing dump that shows request routing metadata.
[03:12] Marta: Is that the standard security pack or a custom package?
[03:16] Jordan: Standard pack plus a short appendix showing the region-pinning controls. We'll add a sample trace that matches your sample traffic.
[03:24] Sofia: On SSO and RBAC, we need SCIM and SAML and ability to limit role-scoped access to specific regions. Is that possible?
[03:34] Priya: We integrate with SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC is resource-scoped. Roles can be limited to org units and projects; for Dedicated/Private we can scope access to specific clusters/regions. For hosted accounts it's more coarse-grained but still project-level.
[03:54] Ethan: What's the audit log retention and can we push logs to our SIEM?
[03:58] Noah: Logs are retained by default for 90 days in hosted; we have long-tail retention as add-on. You can configure log export to your S3/Cloud Storage or push to a SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. For Private deployments you control retention and export.
[04:14] Marta: Subprocessor onboarding is our big concern. If a new CDN or monitoring subprocessor is added, how do we get notified and how soon?
[04:22] Jordan: We do 30-day notice for subprocessor changes by default in our DPA. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate a longer notice period. We'll also post a public subprocessors page and send email notifications to security contacts.
[04:36] Sofia: Do you allow contractual restrictions on certain subprocessors, e.g., block a US-only analytics vendor from touching EU data?
[04:42] Jordan: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can add contractual constraints and operational controls. For hosted, we can offer exclusions in the DPA for specific subprocessors, though some platform dependencies may be hard to replace. We'll surface tradeoffs in the subprocessor inventory.
[04:58] Ethan: If a failover routes to a US-serving plane because EU is maxed, can you ensure the payload is redacted or fails closed? We need to understand data leak risk.
[05:08] Priya: We support a policy layer: fail-closed, fail-open, or route-to-compatible-variant. For sensitive workloads you should pick fail-closed or dedicated capacity. We can also implement request-level redaction rules before routing, but that's more of a customization.
[05:26] Marta: About encryption in transit: do you terminate TLS at Redwood's edge or are we able to use mutual TLS all the way to the serving plane?
[05:34] Noah: We terminate at the edge for hosted, but we support mTLS from your clients to the Redwood edge and then secure internal links. For Private/VPC we can do mTLS end-to-end within your network; certs can be customer-managed.
[05:50] Sofia: Audit question: do your audit logs include routing metadata like region, node id, and subprocessor handling?
[05:56] Priya: Yes, logs include metadata tags: region, logical cluster, model id, and subprocessor proxies involved. The exact fields are in the logging schema doc we'll attach. Note sometimes auto-generated transcripts show slightly different field names, but the data's there.
[06:12] Ethan: Can we run a small deterministic test: 1) pin EU region, 2) send test traffic and capture traces showing region stayed in EU, 3) simulate capacity spike and show fallback behavior?
[06:22] Jordan: Absolutely. That's what the infra deep-dive will prove. Priya/Noah will run a pilot with your topology and provide traces.
[06:30] Priya: For the pilot we'll need an allowlist of your IPs and test credentials. We'll provision a temporary pinned environment and run a short load test to demonstrate behavior; we'll include latency and token-cost numbers.
[06:44] Liam: We'll share the allowlist and a small sample load harness by Monday.
[06:48] Marta: On subprocessors, we have a policy that any subprocessor touching EU personal data cannot be US-located. How do you handle subcontractors of your subprocessors? That's often the blind spot.
[06:58] Jordan: Good point. Our subprocessors list includes second-tier subprocessors where we have visibility. For critical subprocessors we require contractual flow-downs; we can provide attestations and the subprocessor's subcontractor list where available. In some cases we may need to include escrow or specific controls.
[07:16] Sofia: What about legal basis for processing — do you support SCCs for cross-border transfers?
[07:22] Jordan: Yes, we support SCCs and can include a data transfer addendum. For Dedicated/Private often no transfer occurs, but for hosted we have standard SCCs and supplementary measures per EU guidance.
[07:34] Ethan: Is there any fraction of metadata that is always processed outside the EU, e.g., some analytics?
[07:40] Priya: We classify telemetry and payloads separately. By default user payloads follow region pinning; aggregated telemetry may be anonymized and could be processed in the US for analytics unless you opt out. We can opt you out of telemetry export for EU-only customers or route analytics to your EU storage.
[07:58] Marta: Ok, we need two things ASAP: the subprocessors with region mapping and the SOC2 bundle. Also we need the pilot plan.
[08:06] Jordan: Got it. We'll send the pack plus the plan. Anything else?
[08:12] Ethan: A small thing — can you document the timeline for key rotation when using our KMS? We need to align with our rotation policy.
[08:20] Noah: Rotation is managed by your KMS. When keys are rotated, envelope keys are rewrapped; we pick up the new key version on next unwrap operation. We'll document the exact sequence and any temporary dual-key handling in the plan.
[08:36] Sofia: One last question on logging — do you provide immutable logs or support WORM for audit trails?
[08:43] Priya: We can push logs to your S3 with object lock enabled for WORM. For hosted accounts we offer long-term archival options. For Private we recommend configuring your storage with immutability.
[08:58] Jordan: Ok let's recap: Redwood will share subprocessor inventory + DPA excerpt, SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS architecture diagram, and a pilot/test plan. Brighton will provide routing topologies, allowlist, and compliance checklist items. We'll aim to reconvene after the infra deep-dive.
[09:16] Marta: Sounds good, thanks.
[09:18] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email.
[09:22] [meeting ended]

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms like KMS as "K M S" or KV cache as "KV cash", some speaker labels merged (e.g., Jordan/Noah) in auto-transcript; SE clarified a few times. There was minor crosstalk when Ethan and Liam spoke over each other during network details.

Referenced artifacts/links: - Redwood Security Pack (SOC2 + ISO) - Subprocessor inventory (will be attached) - Region-pinning technical appendix - Pilot test plan and load harness (to be shared)

End of transcript.
